context.hint: The baseline asymmetry is known: without a credential the unary listing RPC is rejected while the streaming listing RPC returns a seeded object. A repair is now needed. Which minimal wiring change installs the existing authenticator for streams, does the streaming handler also need the server stream context rather than a fresh background context, and what local matrix distinguishes a complete repair from an auth-only change?
context.surface: Go network service with an in-memory datastore, a reusable preshared-credential authenticator, unary and streaming object-listing handlers, and a disposable local service fixture.
assumptions: The observer can read and modify a disposable local source tree and run the Go toolchain; no public service, production datastore, or live target is used.
The attacker can reach both listing RPCs over the local network and can omit, corrupt, or supply credential metadata; the attacker cannot change server configuration or read the datastore directly.
A valid credential is available for the positive control, and a health RPC has an explicit unary authentication override.
Official benchmark verification is performed outside the producing container; local builds and test logs are evidence for the repair, not an official pass.

incumbent.text: Hypothesis: server startup registers only a unary interceptor chain, so per-stream interceptors are absent and the streaming listing RPC bypasses the authenticator. Prerequisites: preshared-credential service, one seeded tuple, and the ability to call both RPCs without metadata. Bounded test: compare a missing-credential unary listing call with a missing-credential streaming call, recording status and returned identifiers. Expected supporting result: unary is rejected while streaming returns the seeded identifier. Falsifier: both calls are rejected or both are accepted. Cleanup: stop the service and delete the seeded store.

candidates.text: Hypothesis: stream interception alone rejects missing credentials, but the handler still ignores the stream deadline, so a credentialed stream can keep iterating after client cancellation. Prerequisites: patched interception, a seeded many-object store, and a cancelable client context. Bounded test: start a credentialed stream, cancel after the first item, and compare how many items arrive with unary behavior. Expected supporting result: many items arrive after cancellation. Falsifier: the server stops promptly and the context change is unnecessary for lifecycle control. Cleanup: stop the service and delete the store.

Hypothesis: switching the streaming handler from a fresh background context to the server stream context changes lifecycle propagation but not authentication rejection, so both an interceptor and context adoption are required for a complete repair. Prerequisites: patched interceptor logic, a fake server stream carrying a context value, and a datastore stub that can observe the context. Bounded test: run a missing/invalid/valid credential matrix on unary and streaming calls, then call the handler with a fake stream whose context contains a marker and check that the datastore path sees the marker. Expected supporting result: interception rejects bad credentials and the handler observes the stream context. Falsifier: either check fails, or the context change is unnecessary for every observable path. Cleanup: restore the disposable copy.

Hypothesis: chaining stream interceptors globally also covers health or reflection streams and breaks unauthenticated liveness probes. Prerequisites: patched service, health client, and no credential. Bounded test: start the service with preshared authentication, call the health RPC without metadata, then attempt a reflection stream. Expected supporting result: health or reflection fails without a credential. Falsifier: health remains serving and only public data RPCs require credentials. Cleanup: stop the service.

Hypothesis: concurrent stream initialization exposes a race in the new interceptor path, causing occasional unauthenticated disclosures under load. Prerequisites: patched service, seeded store, and many concurrent streams with mixed credentials. Bounded test: launch many concurrent streaming calls, half missing credentials, and count successful disclosures. Expected supporting result: at least one missing-credential stream returns an object. Falsifier: every missing-credential stream is consistently rejected. Cleanup: stop the service and delete the store.

Hypothesis: empty-string, absent, and malformed credential metadata take different extractor branches, so a partial interceptor may reject one form but accept another. Prerequisites: patched service, raw metadata control, and a seeded tuple. Bounded test: call streaming with an absent header, an empty header value, a malformed scheme, and a valid credential, then compare statuses. Expected supporting result: any malformed form is accepted. Falsifier: every non-valid form is rejected. Cleanup: stop the service and delete the store.

evaluations.rationale: Selected. The most complete repair-validation action: it covers the authorization matrix and independently checks that the handler adopts the stream context. It incorporates the baseline evidence while still testing the unexecuted repair.
Incumbent retained. Its baseline bypass is directly observed, but it has low remaining information gain because the next step should move from diagnosis to repair.
Deferred. Useful cancellation discriminator, but its premise that deadline handling is the main remaining defect is secondary; a complete repair should be applied first.
Deferred. Health and reflection regression is important, but the health service has no streaming data RPC and its unary override is already exercised by service startup.
Deferred. A concurrency stress test could reveal races, but it is more expensive and less discriminating than the credential and context matrix.

Ineligible as generated. The core malformed-metadata idea is testable, but the original generation ended in incoherent filler, so it was not used without formalizing a stable hypothesis. It remains a valid alternative for another target.

observation.summary: Applied the minimal repair in the disposable copy: server configuration carries a streaming interceptor chain, startup installs it, the service supplies the same preshared authenticator for streams, and the streaming handler uses the server stream context. The credential matrix passed: missing and invalid credentials were rejected on both unary and streaming calls, while valid credentials returned the seeded object. A separate fake-stream probe injected a marker into the stream context and a datastore stub observed it, confirming context adoption. The package build passed. The first probe run failed only on a capitalization assertion; the failure note and corrected passing log are saved. Local evidence only; official evaluation was not run.
observation.next_hint: Run the host-side official evaluation for the exported patch, then optionally exercise the OIDC authenticator and a no-auth service with the same unary/streaming credential matrix.
